newsitem.title: USA: U.S. suspends military patrols on Mexico border.
newsitem.headline: U.S. suspends military patrols on Mexico border.

text.p: U.S. military drug patrols have been halted along the Texas and New Mexico borders with Mexico following the fatal shooting in May of a teenager herding goats, officials said Thursday.

William Veal, who heads U.S. Border Patrol activities in the region, said soldiers called in to help slow the flow of drugs across the border may have been too aggressive in pursuing suspected traffickers.
"We'd compromise a mission before we provoke a confrontation," Veal said. "We'd rather let that person get away than run the risk of letting someone get hurt or killed."

Texas Rangers were investigating the shooting of 18-year old high school student Esequiel Hernandez, who was tracked and killed by a Marine patrol near Redford, Texas. The Marines said shots were fired by the soldiers in self defence.
"They followed the individual to keep him in their line of sight," said Maureen Boosch, a Marine spokeswoman. "He could've come up on them from another area. They were maintaining their security."

Military activities in the Big Bend area in southwest Texas were suspended immediately after the shooting, and patrols have now been pulled from McAllen, West Texas and New Mexico, Veal said. Two military drug surveillance operations scheduled for New Mexico also were cancelled, he said.

The decision to halt the military patrols comes amid heightened tensions along the border at El Paso. In recent weeks hundreds of random shots have been fired into the city from Cuidad Juarez, and Veal said Mexican police have been slow to respond to reports of the shootings.
"They're not always able to respond," he said "The results are not where we want them to be."
